title: A Statistical Analysis of LLMs' Self-Evaluation Using Proverbs

model.params_source: paper Sec. 4 ('we generate a set of five responses with a temperature setting of 0.7, and generate scores for each response with a temperature setting of 0.0'); max_tokens assumed (the responses are five short sentences)

task.subset_rule: paper-defined subset: the Wisdom-topic proverb pairs whose Siegal-Tukey null hypothesis was rejected for GPT-4 (26 of about 100 pairs); the denominator is itself an outcome of the pipeline, not a fixed split
task.approximation: the 300-pair proverb database is not released, so only the five Wisdom pairs printed in Table 2 are available as items; the five-responses-then-five-scores pipeline is two staged calls per question and is not expressible in the mini-language

items.source: Table 2 of the paper (illustrative pairs only); the full database of 300 proverb pairs / 600 proverbs, built by the authors from public proverb collections (refs 14, 9, 19, 7, 26), is not released - the paper gives no repository, OSF or supplement link

inline.q1: what does the early bird catches the worm mean?
inline.q2: what does the early crow catches the bug mean?

inline.q1: give me a proverb contrary in meaning to faith will move mountains
inline.q2: give me a proverb contrary in meaning to faith will move oceans

inline.q1: give me a proverb contrary in meaning to a miss is as good as a mile
inline.q2: give me a proverb contrary in meaning to a miss is as good as a kilometer

inline.q1: what does one flower does not bring spring mean?
inline.q2: what does two flowers do not bring spring mean ?

inline.q1: why is one never too old to learn?
inline.q2: why is age no barrier to learning?

fields_paper.input: a question q built from an original proverb (Table 1 templates)
fields_paper.paired_input: the question q' built from the manually constructed similar proverb

prompt.system: You are in charge of evaluating the soundness or appropriateness of the '{topic}'. Generate only five short sentences for the given question. Do not add any explanations.
prompt.user_template: What are the best top five short statements to evaluate the following question? Question: {question} Statements:
prompt.source_location: Table 3 ('Prompts for generating responses and scores'), response rows
prompt.verbatim: full (Table 3 as printed; the placeholder <TOPIC> is filled with 'wisdom' and <QUESTION> with the item, per the table caption)

second_stage.system: Evaluate the accuracy score of the "Answer" to the "Question" below using an integer value from 1 to 10. If the "Score" is 10, the "Answer" is completely accurate to the "Question". If the "Score" is 1, the "Answer" is completely inaccurate to the "Question".

output.postprocess: stage 1 returns five short statements; stage 2 returns an integer 1-10 per statement ('number' would parse it)
output.parse_paper: five responses per question, then five integer scores per response; the Siegal-Tukey test is run on the two score vectors S and S' of a proverb pair

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: error rate of the Siegal-Tukey detector: among the proverb pairs whose ST null hypothesis on the raw score vectors is rejected at alpha = 0.05, the share in which a human annotator finds NO scoring failure among the 10 scores. Reported as a fraction, here 1/26 for GPT-4 on the Wisdom topic as judged by Annotator 1.
metric.judge: human (two authors independently inspect every rejected pair for at least one scoring failure; Cohen's kappa 0.469 between them on this cell)
metric.original_location: Table 4, row GPT-4, Wisdom topic, column Anno. 1 (1/26; Anno. 2 gives 3/26)

cost.prepare_note: runner --prepare --dry-run --cap 20 on 2026-09-19 renders the five Table 2 Wisdom items (15 requests, $0.13); this is the illustrative subset only, not the 26-pair claim cell

open_points: data: the 300-pair proverb database (600 proverbs across gender/wisdom/society) is not released and the paper names no repository, so only the handful of pairs printed in Table 2 can be reconstructed. Without the Wisdom pairs the 26-pair denominator cannot be reproduced.

judge: the reported quantity is a human error rate - two annotators decide, per rejected pair, whether any of the 10 scores is a scoring failure. There is no rule or LLM stand-in for that decision, so the cell cannot be recomputed from model output alone.

pipeline: two staged calls per question (generate five statements at T=0.7, then score each at T=0.0) plus a Siegal-Tukey test over the two score vectors; this needs a hook, and the hook is only worth writing once the two points above are settled.
notes: The reproducible part of the pipeline is the ST rejection count itself (a pure function of the generated scores), but the published cell is the human-checked error rate on top of it. Table 5 reports the analogous error rate for the DeBERTa-v3-large NLI textual-consistency variant (potsawee/deberta-v3-large-mnli), which is a live open-weights model but again followed by the same human check.
